days.topic: What Networking Really Is & Why It Matters for Security
objectives: Understand what "What Networking Really Is & Why It Matters for Security" means and where it fits in a real security workflow.
Be able to explain the concept in plain English in under 60 seconds.
Apply the concept once in a hands-on mini-task, not just read about it.
days.theory: Today's focus is **What Networking Really Is & Why It Matters for Security**. Study the core idea in a trusted reference (official docs, a well-known course, or a reputable blog/RFC), taking notes in your own words. Connect it explicitly to the Networking Foundations track and to how it shows up in a junior SOC/cybersecurity/network-security role in practice.
days.practical: Hands-on: apply "What Networking Really Is & Why It Matters for Security" directly inside your lab environment (Packet Tracer / GNS3). Do not just read — configure, run, capture, or script something related to today's topic, and save the evidence (screenshot, command output, or file) for your notebook.
days.challenge: Mini challenge: in 3-4 sentences, explain "What Networking Really Is & Why It Matters for Security" as if you were briefing a non-technical manager.
knowledgeCheck: What is "What Networking Really Is & Why It Matters for Security" and why does it matter for security?
What is one real mistake or misconfiguration related to this topic that you should watch for?
days.career: Directly relevant to Junior SOC Analyst, Network & Security Administrator roles — this is the kind of fundamental interviewers expect you to explain clearly.
